title: Dolphin Emulator graphics settings: “EFB to RAM” vs “EFB to Texture”
summary: Drew Naylor compares Dolphin's EFB-to-RAM and EFB-to-texture paths, a useful illustration of the speed and accuracy tradeoff behind framebuffer copies.
searchKeywords: Dolphin Emulator graphics settings: “EFB to RAM” vs “EFB to Texture”

blocks.text: The embedded framebuffer, or EFB, is part of how GameCube and Wii software moves rendered images into later work. The video explains Dolphin's older EFB-to-RAM and EFB-to-texture settings and uses examples to show why a faster shortcut can differ from a copy visible to the emulated system. It is a focused technical explanation rather than a general setup tutorial, and it helps make sense of effects that depend on reading back an earlier frame.

Dolphin's implementation and menu labels have evolved since this 2016 recording. Use the clip to understand the underlying data path, then consult current documentation before changing a setting by name. If a game has a missing effect, compare the same save and scene with the default configuration first, then a more accurate copy path while recording the performance cost. A higher frame rate is not evidence that the guest saw the data it expected.
